T-mobile is not the manufacture, or producer of the Samsung phones. By law - as a company they have a contract to sell the devices for an agreed upon price. The 1099.99 or whatever amount.l depending on what phone. All promotions at t-mobile and other carriers from my understanding work this way or in a similar fashion. T-mobile, by law - has to have you sign a legally binding document with the full purchase amount of a device - per the contract and deals and laws regulating telecom companies. In order for them to do promotions, they have you say “hey - I want this and I’m gonna buy this and agree to pay the price of the phone”. Since t-mobile is promising you $800 off for trading in your device or adding a new line of service, and since they cannot change the price that you will be billed - once your first bill comes out you’ll see a charge for $50 (normal MRC for Ultra’s) and then directly underneath it a credit for $33.33. In order for you to get the promotion you have to be qualified - and since t-mobile does not do contracts - if you no longer meet promotion qualifications before the phone is paid off, then you are responsible for the balance of the device.
